title: Incident Response Headcount & Hiring
transcript:
Engineering Director: Alright, let's dive into the proposed incident response team expansion. Recruiter, have you found any suitable candidates?

Recruiter: Yes, I've identified a couple of strong candidates for incident response engineers.

Finance Partner: (interrupting) Hang on, before we discuss hiring, let's review the cost implications. If we hire three engineers as suggested, it would exceed our budgeted amounts for integration and restructuring.

Team Lead: I agree with Finance Partner. Our current team is already overextended and cannot handle a significant increase in incidents. The existing system struggles with large volumes.

Engineering Director: I see your point, but we can't afford to wait for final acquisition approval before hiring. The speed of action is critical to minimize potential damage and maintain stakeholder trust.

Finance Partner: Understood, but I still have reservations about hiring more staff before knowing the post-acquisition organizational structure.

Engineering Director: (pausing) I understand your concerns, Finance Partner. We can explore temporary outsourcing as an alternative, but I believe bringing in additional talent in-house will be more effective in the long run.

Recruiter: I suggest we hire two additional incident response engineers for immediate deployment, pending approval of the final acquisition agreement.

Engineering Director: That sounds reasonable. Let's proceed with that plan, provided we can include provisions for increased headcount and budget in the final acquisition agreement.

Finance Partner: (sighs) I'll need to run this by our accounting team and get back to you.

Team Lead: (off-topic) By the way, have you heard about the company-wide picnic next week? I'm thinking of organizing a softball game.

Engineering Director: (smiling) That sounds fun, Team Lead. Let's make sure everyone knows about it and gets a chance to participate.

Acquisition Lead: (entering the room) I've just received the updated agreement. I can sign off on the provisional decision to hire two additional incident response engineers for immediate deployment, subject to final acquisition approval.

All: Thank you, Acquisition Lead.

Title: Meeting Summary - Acquisition Team Discussion

Following the meeting, the decision has been made to hire two additional incident response engineers for immediate deployment, subject to the approval of the final acquisition agreement. The current internal team is stretched thin and unable to handle a significant increase in incidents effectively.

The addition of three engineers was considered, but cost implications would exceed budgeted amounts for integration and restructuring. It was acknowledged that the internal team's capacity is already strained, and further reinforcement is necessary to manage the growing incident load.

No further discussion points will be recorded in this summary.
